=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1534-1554; scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:lines 226-296, 391-408 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: Binding can return ok=true when issue/pull_request reports have no claimed runs or every claimed run is dropped, allowing intake to proceed without verified failed-run evidence.
  WHY: With WORKFLOW_HEAL_REQUIRE_REPORT_AUTH=false, such reports can pass binding and the provenance gate; Qwen says the empty-run behavior predates this PR.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1336-1370 | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The OIDC request URL guard accepts http:// URLs, which could send the bearer token to an arbitrary endpoint if the URL is mis-set.
  WHY: Gemini rates this BLOCKER and Minimax MAJOR; the accepted cleartext scheme risks token exfiltration, though Minimax notes the production runner supplies an HTTPS URL.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1492-1560 | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Autofix reports no longer receive binding-time rejection when claimed runs are all dropped, relying on the downstream provenance gate to reject unverified runs.
  WHY: Gemini rates this BLOCKER and Minimax MAJOR; Minimax notes the downstream gate partly mitigates the risk, while Qwen considers the existing provenance gate sufficient.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:validate_payload(), lines 1231-1232; bind_report_claims(), lines 1518-1525; scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh, lines 1061-1066 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: Binding does not verify report-supplied issue_title, issue_excerpt, or comments_excerpt against GitHub issue data before those fields enter the diagnosis prompt.
  WHY: An unauthenticated sender can name a real labeled issue but supply fabricated excerpts that intake accepts as source context.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1345 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: request_report_identity catches BaseException subclasses such as KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit through its broad except Exception clause.
  WHY: A shutdown during the OIDC request can be suppressed and cause the report to be sent without identity.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:lines 354-372 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The shell run-prefetch kind filter duplicates the Python PROVENANCE_BOUND_KINDS decision, creating a maintenance-drift risk.
  WHY: Changing one of the two decisions without the other can cause unnecessary API calls or leave runs needed for binding unprefetched; Qwen considers this a non-defect API-call optimization.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:line 208 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: workflow_run is listed in PROVENANCE_BOUND_KINDS although the intake does not call bind_report_claims for workflow_run reports.
  WHY: A future call site could pass unverified runs through this membership path without an applicable downstream gate.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Authenticate reports with a per-repository identity or signature, then fetch and bind the claimed issue, label, and failed run to that repository before routing."
  expected_change_site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py::bind_report_claims
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro: bind_report_claims validates the issue and label and filters runs but does not reject an empty filtered run_refs list for issue/pull_request kinds; minimax_minimax-m3: bind_report_claims returns ok=True when kept == [] and intake accepts the report, as asserted by test_intake_binding_rejects_unbacked_claims.
- requirement: Authenticate dispatched reports with GitHub Actions OIDC and bind the claimed repository, issue or PR, label, and failed runs to GitHub data before routing.
  expected_change_site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  EVIDENCE: bind_report_claims allows autofix_failure reports to pass through job validation if they are not verified via the new OIDC identity check while WORKFLOW_HEAL_REQUIRE_REPORT_AUTH=false.

=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1534-1554 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: bind_report_claims returns ok=true with empty run_refs for issue and pull_request reports when every claimed run is dropped; those report kinds skip the intake provenance gate.
  WHY: With WORKFLOW_HEAL_REQUIRE_REPORT_AUTH=false, a report referencing a real issue and label but fabricating all run_refs can reach diagnosis without verified failed-run evidence.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1345 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The broad except Exception in request_report_identity catches BaseException subclasses including KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit.
  WHY: A signal or shutdown during the OIDC request can be suppressed, causing the report to be sent without identity.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Authenticate reports with a per-repository identity or signature, then fetch and bind the claimed issue, label, and failed run to that repository before routing." (linked issue #6559)
  Expected change site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py bind_report_claims return path
  Evidence of absence: The function validates the issue exists, carries the label, and filters runs, but does not reject when the filtered run_refs list is empty for issue/pull_request kinds. These kinds skip the provenance gate that handles other report kinds, leaving no second line of defense against fabricated-run reports.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1336-1370 | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The OIDC request URL guard accepts both https:// and http://.
  WHY: An attacker could influence the URL or intercept traffic to steal the OIDC bearer token, allowing them to bypass identity verification.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1540-1554 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: bind_report_claims() can return ok=true even when all runs are dropped, allowing a report to be processed without a verified failed run.
  WHY: When WORKFLOW_HEAL_REQUIRE_REPORT_AUTH=false (the default), the provenance gate skips binding validation, and the pipeline proceeds with no verifiable failed jobs.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1502-1560 | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: autofix_failure reports skip job validation in bind_report_claims.
  WHY: autofix_failure is not in PROVENANCE_BOUND_KINDS but was incorrectly removed from the filtering logic, potentially allowing reports with successful, non-failing jobs to proceed.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: Authenticate dispatched reports with GitHub Actions OIDC and bind the claimed repository, issue or PR, label, and failed runs to GitHub data before routing.
  Expected change site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py
  Evidence of absence: The PR adds verification of OIDC tokens but the binding logic in bind_report_claims still allows autofix_failure reports to pass through job validation if they are not verified via the new OIDC identity check (if WORKFLOW_HEAL_REQUIRE_REPORT_AUTH=false).
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:lines 1338-1341 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The OIDC request URL guard accepts arbitrary http:// or https:// URLs rather than validating that the endpoint is GitHub's actual endpoint.
  WHY: If ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL is mis-set or influenced by an untrusted context, the bearer token could be exfiltrated and used to mint forged report identities; production GitHub currently supplies an HTTPS endpoint.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:lines 226-296 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: For issue and pull_request reports, intake accepts binding results with an empty run_refs list when every claimed run is dropped.
  WHY: With WORKFLOW_HEAL_REQUIRE_REPORT_AUTH=false, a report naming a real labeled issue or PR can still trigger a heal issue without verified failed-run evidence.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:lines 1492-1559 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The previous binding-time rejection for autofix and workflow_run reports whose claimed runs were all dropped was removed, relying on the downstream provenance gate instead.
  WHY: If that gate misses a case, such as the successful-review-job fallback path, an autofix report with no failed runs can reach log collection and diagnosis; the report notes no test pins rejection of empty run_refs by that gate.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:lines 354-372 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The shell BIND_RUNS_HERE filter duplicates the run-filtering decision represented by PROVENANCE_BOUND_KINDS in Python.
  WHY: The duplication is not a runtime bug today, but future changes to only one decision can desynchronize prefetching and run filtering.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:line 208 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: workflow_run is listed in PROVENANCE_BOUND_KINDS even though the intake does not call bind_report_claims for workflow_run reports.
  WHY: A future call site could pass unverified runs through this membership path and rely on a downstream gate that may not exist.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Authenticate dispatched reports with GitHub Actions OIDC and bind the claimed repository, issue or PR, label, and failed runs to GitHub data before routing."
  Expected change site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py::bind_report_claims for the issue / pull_request branches, OR scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh between the binding block and the provenance block.
  Evidence of absence: bind_report_claims returns {"ok": True, "run_refs": kept, "dropped": dropped} even when kept == [] and the payload had run_refs. The intake accepts the report with report_auth=absent reason=bound (asserted by test_intake_binding_rejects_unbacked_claims). The phrase "failed runs" in the original finding required every claimed run to bind; the implementation only binds runs that happen to match. No diff hunk in workflow_failure_heal.py or workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh rejects label-escalation reports whose claimed run was not found in source_repo (or whose run succeeded); instead those runs are silently dropped and the report is accepted. The earlier reviewer-quoted contract "an autofix report with no bound run is rejected" was removed from README.md in the LAST RUN DIFF without an equivalent run-binding rejection taking its place for label-escalation reports.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:bind_report_claims(), lines 1540-1554; scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh, lines 391-408 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: bind_report_claims() returns ok=true even when every claimed run is dropped, including when the input has no run_refs; the intake writes the empty list back and the provenance gate does not cover issue or pull_request reports.
  WHY: A repository_dispatch report can name an existing issue with the required label but provide no failed run, or only runs that fail binding, and still proceed without verified failed-run evidence.
